'''Bruce Reznick''' (born February 3, 1953, in New York City) is an American mathematician long on the faculty at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]].  He is a prolific researcher<ref>[https://faculty.math.illinois.edu/~reznick/reznickrpubs.html Research Publications of Bruce Reznick] Updated June 29, 2019</ref> noted for his contributions to number theory and the combinatorial-algebraic-analytic investigations of [[polynomial]]s.<ref name=bio>[https://faculty.math.illinois.edu/~reznick/reznicksketch.html Biographical Sketch of Bruce Reznick]</ref>  In July 2019, to mark his 66th birthday, a day long symposium "Bruce Reznick 66 fest: A [[mensch]] of [[Algebraic combinatorics|Combinatorial-Algebraic]] Mathematics" was held at the [[University of Bern]], Switzerland.<ref>[https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~deloera/reznickfest.html Bruce Reznick 66 fest: A mensch of Combinatorial-Algebraic Mathematics] Department of Mathematics, UC Davis</ref>

==Education and career==
Reznick got his B.S. in 1973 from the [[California Institute of Technology]] and his Ph.D. in 1976 from [[Stanford University]] under [[Per Enflo]] for the thesis [https://msp.org/pjm/1978/74-1/pjm-v74-n1-p23-s.pdf "Banach Spaces Which Satisfy Linear Identities"].<ref name=bio/><ref name=mgp>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=4822 Bruce Arie Reznick] at the Mathematics Genealogy Project</ref>

He was a [[Sloan Fellowship|Sloan Fellow]] (1983–1986) and is a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS).<ref name=bio/> From 1983 to 1985 he was on the [[Putnam Competition]] Preparation Committee of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (MAA). As an undergraduate he had been a member of the first place team in the [[Putnam Competition]] twice, also being ranked twice in the top ten as an individual <ref name=bio/>

Reznick is a frequent author on matters relating to teaching and mentoring, and the overall training of graduate students.  He wrote the popular article "Chalking It Up: Advice to a New TA".<ref>[http://bfc.sfsu.edu/cgi-bin/ugpd.pl?Handbooks Resources for Preparing and Supporting Teachers of Undergraduate Mathematics: Handbooks] by Teri Jo Murphy</ref>

==Research==
Reznick has done a systematic analysis of the representation of real forms of even degree as sums of powers of [[linear forms]].  This work was described in his monograph ''Sum of Even Powers of Real Linear Forms'' (Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society, 1992)<ref>''[https://www.amazon.co.uk/Books-Bruce-Reznick/s?rh=n%3A266239%2Cp_27%3ABruce+Reznick Sum of Even Powers of Real Linear Forms]'' by Bruce Reznick, 30 Jul 1992</ref>

Reznick specializes in [[Combinatorial principle|combinatorial methods]] in [[algebra]], [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]] and [[number theory]], often involving polynomials, [[polytope]]s and [[integer sequence]]s.<ref name=claremont>''[http://ccms.claremont.edu/math-colloquium/TBA-2 The secret lives of polynomial identities]'' Speaker Bruce Reznick, [[Claremont Center for the Mathematical Sciences]], September 21, 2011</ref>  He is known for his contributions to the study of sums of squares and positivity of polynomials. In joint work with M.D. Choi and [[T. Y. Lam]], he developed the [[Gram matrix]] method for writing real polynomials as sums of squares; this method has important applications to other areas of mathematics including optimization.<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Xei_K_4AAAAJ&hl=en Google Scholar Citations]  Bruce Reznick, Professor of Mathematics, University of Illinois</ref>

==Awards==
* 2013 fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list Reznick, Bruce, University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign – 2013, Inaugural Class of Fellows] List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society</ref>
* 2008-2009 Campus Award for Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching in the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
* Reznick has an [[Erdős–Bacon number]] of 3 which puts him in a tie for the lead with MIT math professor [[Daniel Kleitman]].<ref>''[https://mitopencourseware.wordpress.com/2016/06/01/math-and-hollywood-mix-it-up-at-mit/ Math and Hollywood mix it up at MIT]'' MIT OpenCourseWare News and Information, June 1, 2016</ref><ref>''Mulcahy, Colm, [https://www.huffpost.com/entry/paul-erdos_b_2945871 Centenary of Mathematician Paul Erdős -- Source of Bacon Number Concept]'' Huffpost, December 6, 2017.  Accessed November 14, 2022.</ref>
